# JPEG inspector fixtures

Tiny synthetic 32 × 24 charts generated by Gazoken. No real camera or personal
metadata is used. All dates, make/model, software labels, and capture settings in
the Exif fixture are deliberately fictitious test values.

| Input | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `baseline-exif.jpg` | Baseline JPEG with common and nested Exif values; orientation 6 also checks that file inspection retains declared frame dimensions without applying pixel rotation. |
| `progressive-optimized.jpg` | Progressive scans and optimized Huffman tables, without Exif. |
| `truncated.jpg` | First 100 bytes of the baseline; an intentionally incomplete structural input. |
| `trailing-data.jpg` | Baseline with the known 20-byte `GAZOKEN_TEST_TRAILER` suffix after EOI. This is a construction example, not evidence that arbitrary trailing bytes are concealed information. |

`expected.json` records checksums, byte lengths, Pillow-extracted quantization
values, dimensions, and progressive flags. These are extraction references, not
expected tampering labels or statistical accuracy results.

Regenerate using Python and Pillow:

```bash
python3 tests/generate_jpeg_fixtures.py
```

Generation overwrites these named fixtures and `expected.json`. The environment
and JPEG codec version are recorded in that JSON. Encoded bytes can vary with
Pillow or codec versions. Parser checks run with `node tests/jpeg.test.mjs`;
UI checks are available at `tests/jpeg-browser.html` through a local HTTP server.
